problem: Two-stage waypoint-based VLN-CE methods suffer from global sub-optimality (proxy objectives per stage) and are bottlenecked by the quality of the predicted waypoints; end-to-end BC policies in continuous space suffer compounding error and underperform.
motivation: If the waypoint predictor produces no waypoint toward the goal (e.g. stairs), the agent cannot recover. An end-to-end policy that captures multi-modal actions (ambiguous instructions, equivalent paths) and learns error recovery could remove this bottleneck.
key_idea: Replace the waypoint predictor plus planner with a single instruction-conditioned diffusion policy that samples the next action in continuous space, trained with DAgger to learn error recovery.
insight: DAgger is essential for end-to-end diffusion policies: without it SR is 21.0 and collisions are 238.2, with it SR reaches 83.3 (alpha=0.10, Table 5). Lower alpha (more agent freedom) gives higher SR but longer trajectories and lower SPL. Short history (3 latest observations) beats longer or sparse history, and a normalized-distance stop predictor beats classification stop, which suffers from class imbalance.
method: State encoder: CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB + depth encoder + heading-angle embeddings feed a panorama transformer; history waypoint embeddings (distance, heading, step) attend to instruction (LXMERT) in a cross-modal transformer to give state S_t

Conditional diffusion policy: NoMaD-style 1D conditional U-Net noise predictor, K=10 denoising steps, conditioned on S_t, predicts next action (sequence length 1) in continuous space, trained with MSE noise loss
Temporal distance predictor: MLP on S_t regresses normalized distance to goal, used for stopping; loss weight lambda=1e-4
Sparse demonstration trajectories: sub-sample expert paths every n=2 steps (0.5 m spacing) to enlarge the action range; only 3 latest observations as history

DAgger-boosted online training: in Habitat, execute the policy with prob. and query the expert (action minimizing geodesic distance to the expert trajectory) otherwise; 5 rounds; aggregate trajectories, then fine-tune

setting.backbone: Diffusion policy (1D U-Net) + cross-modal transformer state encoder with CLIP ViT-B/32, depth encoder and LXMERT (frozen encoders), trained
setting.training_data: R2R-CE expert demonstrations plus DAgger-aggregated online trajectories; per-scene training for the environment-category experiments
setting.action_space: continuous next-action sampled from the diffusion policy (waypoint-like displacement, 0.5 m spacing), low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° in the base task
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert demonstrator with geodesic info only during DAgger training)

numbers.eval_set_note: One randomly selected scene per category (Open Area), model trained only on that scene's data; not the full split
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (R2R-CE results), Open Area, DifNav(Ours): 2.2 / 90.5 / 90.5 / 89.7 (SRL column)

numbers.eval_set_note: One randomly selected Narrow Space scene, trained only on that scene
One randomly selected Stairs scene, trained only on that scene

numbers_note: The paper reports no full R2R-CE val-unseen/test results; only per-scene subset results (21/15/21 episodes-scale) and ablations (e.g. 3 latest observations: NE 1.7, OSR 94.4, SR 91.4, SRL 88.8), whose split and eval set are unspecified. The SRL column is taken as SPL.
results: On small per-scene subsets (open area, narrow space, stairs), DifNav reaches SR 90.5/93.3/90.5, beating the best two-stage baseline BEVBert (SR 66.7/80/85.7) and the best end-to-end continuous baseline WS-MGMap. DAgger raises SR from 21.0 to 83.3 in the ablation.
limitations: Evaluation is on tiny hand-picked single-scene subsets rather than standard R2R-CE val-unseen/test, so comparability with published SOTA is unclear
Lower DAgger alpha yields longer trajectories and lower SPL; hyperparameters (waypoint spacing, history length) are sensitive
Only R2R-CE is evaluated; no real-robot experiments
